subject: On-prem data path qualification + action items (post-demo)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <epark@healertech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem data path qualification + action items (post-demo)

Hi Elena / HealerTech security team —

Thanks again for carving out time for the demo this morning. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key data-flow constraints and our proposed next steps so we can qualify the Private/VPC path for your use case. TL;DR: we believe Redwood Private can meet your air-gapped ingestion and PII residency needs, but we need a quick confirmation on two technical points below to finalize a scoped runbook.

Recap of constraints you called out:
- Ingest from on-prem batch jobs only (no persistent outbound tunnels from your production network).
- All PII must remain within your US datacenter region and be deleted after 30 days unless flagged for retention.
- Syslog/IDS events must be forwarded to your SIEM; we cannot ship raw request logs outside your VPC.
- For the prototype, you want an air-gapped path with manual deploys and HSM-backed keying.

Open items / asks (owners + ETA):
1) Network boundary: confirm whether the batch jobs will push to an internal S3-compatible endpoint (preference) or to an on-prem HTTP gateway. If S3 endpoint, please share bucket naming and region. (Action: Elena — reply by 2027-04-14)
2) Egress policy: can your infra team allow outbound TLS to a private peering endpoint (no public IPs) or must we use physical media transfers for initial model weights? Clarify both pilot and production policies. (Action: Tom / security — reply by 2027-04-14)
3) Logging retention: you requested request-level masking and retention for 30 days; please confirm the allowed fields we may persist in application logs (e.g., request_id, model_id, latency_ms) and which fields must be redacted. (Action: HealerTech Security — reply by 2027-04-16)
4) Crypto/KMS: confirm HSM vendor and whether you require an on-prem HSM or if cloud KMS within your VPC is acceptable for prototype. (Action: Ben — coordinate with infra; Ben to deliver options doc by 2027-04-15)
From: Elena Park <epark@healertech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealerTech Security <security@healertech.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@consults.net>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem data path qualification + action items (post-demo)

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Ingest path: for the pilot we can push batches to an internal minio S3 endpoint (same cluster as prod), so S3-compatible is preferred. I will pull the bucket details tomorrow.
- Egress: production security policy forbids any persistent outbound connection from prod nodes to public endpoints. Private direct-peering (VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink equivalent) to a peering endpoint hosted in our co-lo is acceptable for production. For the pilot, we can open a temporary peering tunnel. No physical media transfers — too slow.
- Logs: we must redact user PII (name, ssn, email) from stored request bodies. Request metadata (request_id, timestamp, model_id, token_count) is fine. We will not allow raw prompt storage unless explicitly flagged.
- HSM: vendor is Thales; we prefer an on-prem HSM for production. For the pilot, a cloud KMS within our VPC (customer-managed keys) would be acceptable if envelope encryption is used.

I'll attach a rough data-map and our security checklist.

Thanks,
Elena

---
Attachments: healertech-data-map-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <epark@healertech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem data path qualification + action items (post-demo)

Appreciate the fast turn, Elena — exactly what we needed. I pulled out the immediate implementation path based on your answers:

Pilot (2–4 weeks):
- Ingest: Redwood will accept batch uploads to an internal S3-compatible endpoint via a private peering endpoint. We will provide a presigned-upload helper that runs within your network (no public egress).
- Keys & crypto: use AWS KMS customer-managed key in your VPC; Redwood will support envelope encryption. We will not persist plaintext model inputs.
- Logging: Redwood will redact prompt bodies by default and retain request metadata for 30 days. We will provide a masked-request sample to validate.
- Deployment: manual, scheduled deploys with no inbound control-plane traffic from the public internet; control plane operates over the peering link.

Production (Q3 target):
- Migrate to Thales HSM integration for key ops; audited key usage logs will be delivered to your SIEM via syslog over an internal collector.
- Full air-gap readiness: a validated runbook for offline model updates (signed artifacts on USB transferred via Ops) if required.

Action items I will follow up on this week:
- Ben: produce a short PKI/HSM options matrix (redwood-pki-checklist.xlsx) showing cloud-KMS vs. Thales integration and operational steps.
- Marissa: will scope a minimal SOC-like runbook for the pilot (access controls, approval gates).
- Elena / HealerTech: share the exact bucket name and the SIEM syslog endpoint.

If that roadmap matches your expectations I can convert to a mutual action plan and push to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — Jordan

---
Attachments: redwood-pki-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem data path qualification + action items (post-demo)

Quick note — I started the PKI/HSM options matrix. Two immediate follow-ups I want to highlight: 
- If they use Thales on-prem HSM, we'll need an offline key-wrapping step in the pipeline (Ben -> Elena: can you confirm Thales model and whether remote key signing is allowed?).
- For the pilot cloud-KMS option, we recommend using a customer-managed key with an HSM-backed provider and enable envelope encryption; this keeps plaintext out of Redwood storage.

I'll have the spreadsheet and a short narrative uploaded to the Drive link by EOD.

—Ben
From: Elena Park <epark@healertech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealerTech Security <security@healertech.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@consults.net>
Date: Thu, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem data path qualification + action items (post-demo)

Jordan / Ben —

This roadmap looks good. Two quick items:
1) Bucket: healertech-prod-uploads (us-west-2). I'll share an IAM minimal role for presigned uploads tomorrow.
2) Thales model: nShield-800; remote key signing is supported but must be limited to a jump-host inside our security zone. We'll confirm the HSM admin contact.

Please move the mutual action plan to HubSpot when you're ready and we can lock in a pilot kickoff next week.

Best,
Elena
